name: Eric Clapton
hook: A blues guitarist who left the Yardbirds for being too pop, was shaken by seeing Jimi Hendrix, and whose 1976 onstage support for Enoch Powell set off Rock Against Racism.
blurb: Eric Clapton was born in Ripley, Surrey, in 1945. He joined the Yardbirds in October 1963 and left in March 1965 because the band was moving towards pop. His time in John Mayall's Bluesbreakers (1965 to 1966) made his name on the club circuit, and Cream (1966 to 1968), with Jack Bruce and Ginger Baker, made him a star. On 1 October 1966 Jimi Hendrix sat in with Cream at the Central London Polytechnic, which Wikipedia's article on Clapton describes as having an immediate and major effect on his playing. In August 1976, at a concert in Birmingham, Clapton spoke in support of Enoch Powell, a politician known for speeches against immigration, and made racist statements about immigrants. Angry letters in response led to the founding of Rock Against Racism, whose founders say it was the event that turned their idea into a campaign. That is part of why his name sits on this map next to the punk scene as well as the blues.
